A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AIRA research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across appendix renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent evaluations on MLE-bench Lite, controlled ablations, validation/test comparisons, and extended-runtime experiments, including results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds the authors' full-suite AIRA evaluation in Appendix D, separately identifying reproduced baseline results.

M1.justification: The search policies, operator design, fitness evaluation, and selection procedures are retained. Appendix E.6 newly documents the crossover prompt, but crossover and fitness-based parent selection already appeared in v1; this does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Appendix D expands actual evaluation from 22 low-complexity Lite tasks to all 75 MLE-bench tasks, adding 38 medium- and 15 high-complexity competitions. Added coverage includes multilingual question answering, recommendations, and autonomous-vehicle object detection. MLE-bench-30 is also reported as a subset of this coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 2 adds OpenAI's proprietary o3 and GPT-5 Thinking agents, both without browsing, as reported comparators on MLE-bench-30, with scores of 6% and 8%. These are distinct from the existing AIDE/AIRA o3 configurations. The original controlled comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D reports additional o3 runs using high reasoning effort and improved filesystem/model caching, explicitly linking these configuration changes to the new Lite result. The original main experiments, medal metrics, and stated 24-hour, single-GPU protocol are retained.

E4.justification: The memory and search-policy ablations, extended-compute studies, validation/test and top-k analyses, variance analyses, and search-tree examples are retained. Appendix D adds benchmark and difficulty-group scores without introducing a new ablation, sensitivity test, error analysis, or case study.

E5.justification: The added full-suite evaluation states 20 random seeds, whereas the retained o3 Lite results specify 10 seeds in Figures 13–14. Table 2 introduces mean ± standard-error reporting alongside the existing bootstrap confidence intervals. Appendix D inconsistently calls its uncertainty estimates confidence intervals in prose.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports AIRA greedy o3 medal rates of 31.6% overall, 55.0% low, 22.0% medium, 21.7% high, and 25.8% on MLE-bench-30; Table 3 adds 75 task-level results. The 55.0% result uses updated settings relative to the original 47.7%. Section 5.3 also corrects the oracle-selection gain from 9–11.6 to 9–13 points, while Figure 6 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: The graph-search definitions, selection equations, UCT formulation, and MCTS backup derivation are unchanged. The backup discussion moves from Appendix D.1 to E.1; no new theorem, assumption, proof, or substantive mathematical revision is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a claim of 55% Lite performance with updated AIRA-dojo and announces full-suite results. The central contributions concerning search/operator interactions and generalization remain unchanged, as do the abstract and conclusion's original 47.7% headline.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly attributes the additional Lite performance to high reasoning effort and infrastructure improvements, including caching to avoid rate-limit errors. Their individual contributions are not isolated. Existing interpretations of overfitting and the limitations concerning resources, operators, and contamination remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E.6 supplies the previously omitted crossover prompt, including parent-code inputs, memory, constraints, and output format. Appendix D adds information about reasoning effort, infrastructure updates, and baseline-result provenance. Existing hardware specifications, other prompts, hyperparameters, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the GPT-5 system card as a cited source for MLE-bench-30 and proprietary-agent comparisons. The existing related-work discussion and novelty framing are largely unchanged; the added Inspect publication date is only a bibliographic update.

P1.justification: Changes include a short introduction addition, localized wording and author/date edits, new Appendix D and subsection E.6, and updated appendix references. Most prose and the main section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds an aggregate comparison table and a full per-task table with complexity groups, years, and MLE-bench-30 markers, plus crossover prompt boxes. Existing Figures 1–17 are preserved, with some appendix material relocated and repaginated.

improvement.justification: Appendix D substantially strengthens empirical validation beyond v1's low-complexity Lite tasks: the 20-seed full-suite evaluation establishes performance on harder problem types and exposes task-level failures. The crossover prompt also improves reproducibility. Combined reasoning/infrastructure changes limit attribution of the 55% result, and the SE/CI terminology needs clarification, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gain in evidence about the agent's applicability.
